tasks.title: Add account and credit persistence foundation
tasks.objective: Extend the existing lofi local and Supabase persistence boundaries with users, hashed sessions, immutable credit transactions, purchases, processed Stripe events, nullable account links, and atomic credit primitives.
write_scope: account, session, credit, purchase, and Stripe-event domain records
local store and repository persistence
credit ledger and balance service
additive cohort15_lofi_* Supabase migration and adapter mappings
focused persistence, migration, balance, concurrency, and idempotency tests
src/persistence/README.md
authority: Create only additive cohort15_lofi_* objects and nullable creator_user_id/user_id links; do not drop, rename, or rewrite existing production rows.
Persist only SHA-256 session-token digests and private CSRF verification material, never raw session tokens.
Use immutable positive-integer grant, purchase, hold, consume, and refund entries; do not add a mutable balance column.
Provide transaction-safe primitives for account-plus-signup-grant provisioning, credit holds, quorum consumption, expiry refunds, and purchase fulfillment.
Enforce unique normalized email, Supabase subject, ledger idempotency key, provider checkout ID, purchase credit transaction, and Stripe event ID constraints.
Keep all new tables RLS-enabled with no browser policies and revoke public execution of security-definer functions.
Do not add HTTP routes, auth UI, Stripe network calls, or live provider changes in this task.
acceptance_criteria: Local and Supabase repositories expose equivalent user, session, credit transaction, purchase, and Stripe-event behavior.
Account provisioning can atomically create or find a user and add exactly one two-credit signup grant.
Balance derivation reports funded, available, held, consumed, and refunded totals and cannot become negative.
Hold, consume, and refund primitives reject insufficient or missing holds and are safe under concurrent calls.
Existing cohort/interest rows with null user IDs remain readable and participate in existing quorum counts without credit transactions.
The additive migration preserves existing lofi tables/data, uses a safe function search path, RLS, service-role-only execution, and all documented uniqueness constraints.
Focused tests cover duplicate signup grants, concurrent holds, duplicate consume/refund, purchase idempotency, legacy null links, serialization, and migration isolation.
verification: Run focused persistence, credit ledger, and Supabase adapter tests
Inspect the additive migration for destructive SQL, unsafe grants, mutable balances, and non-lofi objects
tasks.stop_condition: Stop when the durable data and transaction boundary is verified; leave authentication, product routes, and Stripe HTTP integration to later tasks.
tasks.evidence: Implemented local and Supabase users, digest-only sessions, immutable credit ledger, derived balances, purchases, Stripe-event receipts, nullable account links, and atomic provisioning/hold/settlement/fulfillment primitives. Added the isolated additive migration and focused concurrency, replay, privacy, adapter, and migration tests. npm run check passed with 88 tests on 2026-07-15 EDT.
tasks.notes: Completed without HTTP routes, auth UI, Stripe network calls, or live provider changes. Concepts from main were consulted only as read-only reference and adapted to the lofi repository interfaces.

tasks.title: Implement magic-link accounts and signup credits
tasks.objective: Add production Supabase email magic-link sign-in, opaque persisted application sessions, CSRF protection, sign-out, and the exactly-once two-credit signup grant.
write_scope: Supabase magic-link auth adapter
application session and CSRF service
sign-in, callback, and sign-out routes
auth UI and shared navigation state
local test-auth support
auth/session runtime configuration
focused auth, session, privacy, and grant tests
authority: Implement email magic links only; do not add passwords, Google, GitHub, profiles, or account management.
Use verified Supabase identity data as the only production account-provisioning authority.
Provision the account and two-credit signup grant through the L015 atomic primitive; callback replay and concurrent callbacks must not duplicate grants.
Use opaque eight-hour sessions with hashed persisted tokens and Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax production cookies.
Require CSRF for authenticated browser mutations and validate all return paths as safe relative application paths.
Return generic magic-link request responses and never log emails, auth tokens, session tokens, CSRF tokens, or provider bodies.
Do not gate cohort creation/interest or add Stripe checkout in this task.
acceptance_criteria: Production sign-in requests a Supabase email magic link without revealing account existence.
A verified callback creates or finds the application account, ensures exactly one two-credit grant, creates a durable app session, and redirects safely.
Repeated login, callback replay, concurrent callbacks, and an existing account missing its grant result in exactly one signup grant total.
Signed-in navigation shows the account's available credits and Buy Credits/sign-out actions without exposing the email publicly.
Expired, unknown, or signed-out sessions fail closed; sign-out deletes the session and clears the cookie.
Production local seeded-account selection is absent, while injected local test identity keeps automated tests provider-independent.
Focused tests cover cookie attributes, session expiry, CSRF, unsafe returns, generic responses, privacy, and provider failures.
verification: Run focused Supabase auth and session-security tests
Run route tests for sign-in, callback, replay, and sign-out
tasks.stop_condition: Stop when account/session behavior and signup credits are verified without changing cohort mutation semantics.
tasks.evidence: Implemented dependency-free Supabase magic-link request/verification, atomic account and signup-grant provisioning, opaque eight-hour digest-backed sessions, CSRF-protected sign-out, safe returns, shared balance/navigation UI, injected test auth, anon-key runtime configuration, and privacy-safe failure handling. npm run check passed with 93 tests on 2026-07-15 EDT.
tasks.notes: Completed without changing cohort creation/interest semantics or adding Stripe behavior. Human Supabase Auth, email-template, key, and callback configuration remains in docs/human-tasks/piece-of-pie-launch.md.

tasks.title: Credit-gate cohort creation and interest
tasks.objective: Require authenticated accounts and atomic credit holds for cohort creation and interest, then consume at quorum and refund at below-quorum expiry while preserving the public lofi experience.
write_scope: authenticated create and interest service orchestration
atomic local/Supabase hold, quorum-consume, and expiry-refund integration
create/detail forms and insufficient-credit notices
server routes and session/CSRF enforcement
notification identity integration
focused product credit, lifecycle, concurrency, privacy, and regression tests
authority: Keep public browsing, schedules, filters, research, feedback, and public meeting-link timing unchanged.
Derive creator and participant email from the authenticated account; remove editable email fields for new mutations.
Hold exactly two credits with successful creation and one with accepted interest in the same transaction.
Reject insufficient credits with HTTP 402 and a clear Buy Credits action without creating a record or hold.
Consume account-backed holds once at quorum and lazily refund below-quorum holds once before balance reads or funded mutations.
Preserve legacy anonymous rows with null user IDs; do not claim, backfill, grant, hold, consume, or refund credits for them.
Preserve existing validation, honeypot, rate-limit, media-type, body-size, Origin, email-notification, and privacy boundaries.
Do not add Stripe network behavior in this task.
acceptance_criteria: Anonymous visitors can browse but must sign in before opening the create flow or submitting interest.
A new two-credit account can create exactly one cohort and then encounters the payment gate for another funded action.
Accepted interest holds one credit; duplicates, creator self-interest, expired/already-met cohorts, and rejected requests create no hold.
Exactly one concurrent interest request reaches quorum and consumes each account-backed hold once.
Below-quorum expiry refunds creator and participant holds once through lazy settlement and restores available balance.
Existing anonymous data and current public rendering remain intact, and notifications use the private authenticated email.
Focused tests cover insufficient balance, concurrent actions, rollback, quorum, expiry, legacy rows, CSRF, rate limits, and public privacy.
verification: Run focused create, interest, credit lifecycle, notification, and Supabase concurrency tests
Run the local account-to-create and account-to-interest browser flow
tasks.stop_condition: Stop when free credits fund the real cohort flow and insufficient balance reaches a non-functional Buy Credits gate; Stripe belongs to L018.
tasks.evidence: Implemented authenticated and CSRF-protected create/interest routes, private account-derived identity, atomic local/Supabase create-plus-hold and interest-plus-hold operations, quorum consumption, lazy expiry refunds, HTTP 402 Buy Credits gates, and legacy/public behavior preservation. Focused persistence, concurrency, route, notification, migration, privacy, and browser-flow checks passed; npm run check passed with 94 tests on 2026-07-15 EDT.
tasks.notes: Completed without Stripe network behavior or public-content redesign. Existing anonymous rows remain nullable and continue to participate in public lifecycle/quorum behavior without credit transactions.

tasks.title: Implement Stripe checkout and idempotent fulfillment
tasks.objective: Add one authenticated USD $6/six-credit Stripe Checkout package with signed webhooks, verified browser-return reconciliation, and exactly-once purchase credit fulfillment.
write_scope: Stripe HTTP and signature-verification adapter
purchase checkout and fulfillment service
Buy Credits, checkout, webhook, and completion routes
one-package payment UI
Stripe runtime configuration and non-secret templates
focused adapter, signature, route, purchase, idempotency, and failure tests
authority: Offer only six credits for USD $6 through a server-selected configured Stripe Price ID.
Use Stripe-hosted Checkout; never receive or persist card data.
Persist a pending purchase before Checkout Session creation and set server-owned user/purchase metadata and provider idempotency key.
Verify the raw webhook signature and five-minute timestamp tolerance before parsing or acting; limit webhook bodies to 256 KiB.
Accept only completed, paid sessions matching stored checkout ID, metadata, user, amount, currency, and package.
Route webhook and server-retrieved browser return through one transaction-safe, idempotent fulfillment service.
Cancellation, unpaid, mismatched, invalid-signature, wrong-owner, and provider-failure paths grant no credits.
Do not log secrets, full provider payloads, card data, emails, session cookies, or Checkout URLs.
acceptance_criteria: A signed-in user can start the configured six-credit Checkout and an anonymous or CSRF-invalid request cannot.
The browser cannot control price, amount, currency, quantity, user ID, purchase ID, or redirect origins.
A valid paid webhook adds one six-credit purchase transaction and marks the purchase paid.
Duplicate events, concurrent webhook/return calls, webhook retries, and completion-page refreshes cannot add credits more than once.
The completion route retrieves Stripe state server-side, verifies ownership, invokes shared fulfillment, and renders paid/pending/failure safely.
Invalid signatures return 400, unknown valid events return 200, retryable internal failures return 500, and cancellation grants nothing.
Automated tests use fake Stripe transports and secrets and make no live provider calls.
verification: Run focused Stripe adapter, webhook signature, checkout, fulfillment, and route tests
Inspect logs/errors and fixtures for secret, email, card, and provider-payload leakage
tasks.stop_condition: Stop when local/fake-provider checkout and fulfillment are money-safe and tested; leave real dashboard configuration and live payment to L020.
tasks.notes: The incomplete browser-return payment concepts on main are reference material only; signed webhook reliability is mandatory here.
